RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Emerson Lawson
Member ID: W445912797
Reference Number: POC-5717F9EEEF-88905
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-02
Requested Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 23472 (total/reverse shoulder arthroplasty), issued in the notice dated 2026-08-02. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in the denial notice, which specifies that an appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (by 2027-01-29).

The plan has identified that its medical-necessity review for this procedure is governed by Medical Policy MP430, "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty." I understand from that policy that initial shoulder joint replacement, including CPT 23472, "may be considered medically necessary... when all the following criteria are met: A. There is no active infection in the shoulder joint; and B. At least two of the following are met (1.-3.) 1. Pain interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs); or 2. Pain is increased with initiation of activity; or 3. Pain occurs with range of motion (ROM); and C. Imaging confirms any of the following (1.-6.)... 6. Osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis and the following criteria are met (a.-b.): a. Member has either limited range of motion or crepitus with glenohumeral joint rotation; and b. Either of the following are met: i. Imaging shows bone-on-bone contact; or ii. Member has continued symptoms despite conservative treatments within the last year and at least two of the following are present..."

The policy also states that, to determine medical necessity, "the following information must be submitted in order to determine if medical necessity criteria are met: Indication for the requested surgery; Clinical documentation of extent and response to conservative care, as applicable to the policy criteria, including outcomes of any procedural interventions, medication use and physical therapy notes; Evaluation and documentation of the extent and specifics of one or more of the functional impairments or disabilities...; Imaging requirements: Imaging completed within the past 12 months, Documented interpretation of x-rays, which may be performed and read by the operating surgeon, If advanced imaging is required, a radiologist's report (for CT, MRI, US or bone scan)... Documentation of any criteria-specific lab values or reports."

The medical record already in the plan's possession, and re-submitted with this appeal, addresses each of these elements directly:

1. No active infection (Criterion A): The record documents "No active infection" in the shoulder joint at the time of evaluation.

2. Pain/functional criteria (Criterion B): The record documents that Mr./Ms. Lawson "cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side," which reflects pain interfering with activities of daily living. The record also documents glenohumeral crepitus on examination, reflecting pain occurring with range of motion. This satisfies at least two of the three listed indicators under Criterion B.

3. Imaging criteria for osteoarthritis (Criterion C.6): Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) obtained 2026-05-21 are documented as showing "complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid." This finding of complete joint space loss reflects bone-on-bone contact, which the policy lists as sufficient under Criterion C.6.b.i. Examination findings of glenohumeral crepitus and active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees satisfy Criterion C.6.a (limited range of motion and/or crepitus with glenohumeral joint rotation). CT imaging confirming an intact rotator cuff was also obtained and is available to the plan.

4. Documentation of conservative care (supporting the Documentation Requirements section and demonstrating the extent of prior treatment): The record documents 9 months of progressive shoulder pain unrelieved by rest; 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-04-11 through 2026-06-06) focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-22 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.

5. Imaging timing: The radiographs and CT referenced above were obtained on 2026-05-21, which is within the policy's requirement that "Imaging completed within the past 12 months."

Given that the imaging findings independently satisfy Criterion C.6.b.i (bone-on-bone contact), and Criteria A and B are also documented in the record, I ask that the plan reconsider this denial based on the complete clinical documentation enclosed, which includes:

- Office visit notes from Dr. Duval, MD, documenting symptom duration, functional limitations, and examination findings
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-11 to 2026-06-06)
- Medication history documenting NSAID use and the 2026-03-22 corticosteroid injection and its outcome
- Radiology report for shoulder radiographs dated 2026-05-21
- CT imaging report confirming rotator cuff integrity
- [Any additional operative planning notes or letters of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, MD, not already on file]

If any specific document or data element is still considered missing by the plan, I respectfully request that the plan identify the exact missing item(s) so that Dr. Duval's office can supply them promptly, given the appeal deadline of 2027-01-29.

I am also requesting, pursuant to my appeal rights, a copy of the specific clinical review criteria (including any InterQual® or other guideline excerpts) that were applied to my case, as referenced in Medical Policy MP430.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed. Dr. Duval's office may be reached at [surgeon's office phone number] and can provide any additional records requested.

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this appeal.

Sincerely,

Emerson Lawson
Member ID: W445912797

Enclosures: [List of enclosed medical records]

cc: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [office address/fax, if to be copied]
